To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the integrated observables σ + and σ – can be used to derive model-independent limits on the four-fermions contact interactions, and that the use of longitudinal polarization of the e-beam is essential to obtain such limits.

the sensitivity to contact interactions is enhanced by the use of longitudinal polarization and that, in this way and for a given luminosity, it is possible to obtain model-independent bounds on contact interactions.

the observables σ + and σ – are sensitive to the helicity cross section and that the bounds derived on the parameters λ LL, λ LR, λ RL and λ RR can be interpreted as model-independent limits on four fermion contact interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of a model-independent analysis of the contact interaction parameters, based on the use of polarization and the observables σ + and σ –. The analysis has been performed in the framework of an effective Lagrangian approach, where the four-fermions contact interactions are described by a dimension six operator.

the following issues: (i) the determination of the optimal values of the polarization of the beams; (ii) the definition of a suitable set of integrated observables to be used for the extraction of the helicity cross section; (iii) the definition of the optimal set of parameters that describe the four-fermions contact interactions; (iv) the derivation of model-independent bounds on these parameters.
the possibility to obtain information on new interactions by means of the polarization of the initial electron beam.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, if longitudinal beam polarization were available, the model-independent sensitivity of future e + e - colliders would improve by a factor 2-4 with respect to the case without polarization.

a 500 GeV LC, equipped with longitudinal polarization, would be able to probe the four-fermions contact interactions with a sensitivity comparable to the one of the LEP2 experiments, and that, at the same time, the same machine would be able to reach the sensitivity of the LHC experiments in the case of the contact interaction between the top and the bottom quarks.
the sensitivity of σ + and σ – to four-fermi contact interactions would be comparable to, or even better than, the one of the total cross section σ T.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for the considered processes, a 90% CL bound on the scale of the contact interaction Λ can be obtained by measuring the integrated cross sections for unpolarized beams and for the longitudinal polarization of one beam, and by comparing the two values.

, for the processes under consideration, the use of the σ + and σ− observables, together with the longitudinal polarization of the e + beam, would allow us to derive bounds on the four-fermions contact interaction parameters which are more than one order of magnitude better than those obtained from the unpolarized cross sections alone.

the sensitivity of the integrated observables σ +, σ −, and the helicity cross section asymmetry A LL to four-fermite contact interactions is comparable to the one of the integrated cross section, and that the polarization of the electron beams is crucial to extract the helicity cross-section information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the polarization of the initial beam can be a powerful tool to probe new physics, in the case of the four-fermions contact interactions.
the sensitivity to new physics in these observables is significantly enhanced by the availability of longitudinal polarization.
the use of polarization can be crucial in the analysis of contact interaction effects in e + e − collisions.
